implementation: Selective Pressure Allocation Section 6.3.2, Eqs. 26 and 49-52; Gaussian exploration from Yahyaa et al. (2014), Section 4.2.

bandit.initialization_note: Repeat the entire Eq. 43 arm-direction schedule twice: 100 initialization requests, then 50 adaptive KG requests.
bandit.cost_reference_note: Fixed lower reference in normalized cost coordinates, strictly below nonnegative observations (Eq. 24). Distinct from the upper total-cost hypervolume reference.
bandit.observation_bounds_note: Overhead: M times the largest float32 class policy payload in KiB. Instability: 1. Observations are normalized costs, not one-minus-cost rewards.
bandit.kg_index: se * (phi(q) - q * Phi(-q)); q = abs(mean - minimum_other_arm_mean) / se
bandit.exploration_note: B = (T-k)*K*D*v from the original scalarized KG exploration bound; k is the upcoming one-based global request. D=2 in both variants. The final request has zero bonus.

evaluation.note: Approximate the exponential set of all horizon-length sequences over the currently recommended arms using 16 sampled sequences and all constant sequences; deduplicate. Reuse identical held-out scenario seeds and Sobol draws across subsets, formulations, and gravity levels. Cache repeated subsets. Evaluation observations never update the bandit.
evaluation.hypervolume_note: Empirical RTS/STR polar hypervolume of the sampled sequence set, using the same fixed total-cost reference as MORBO/qNParEGO. Plot current estimates, without a cumulative maximum.

horizon_note: 150 online training requests are necessary because KG needs 2*10*5=100 initialization requests. Held-out evaluation sequences retain length 100 and the original total-cost reference, matching holistic UCB/MORBO/qNParEGO.
comparison_note: KG follows the paper cost-minimization max-length scalarization. Existing UCB uses min-length scalarization of one-minus-cost rewards. Their optimizer conventions differ; this pilot is not a controlled ranking. UCB results are preserved.

original_paper.title: Knowledge Gradient for Multi-objective Multi-armed Bandit Algorithms
